summary.text: Amines are organic compounds that contain carbon–nitrogen bonds.
They form when one or more hydrogen atoms in ammonia are replaced by alkyl or aryl groups.
Amines are classified as primary, secondary or tertiary, and the nitrogen atom in an amine has a lone pair of electrons.

facts.label: Simplest aromatic amine
facts.value: Aniline, a benzene ring with an amino group

facts.label: Amino group
facts.value: The −NH₂ group found in primary amines

facts.label: Quaternary ammonium
facts.value: Four organic substituents on the nitrogen

items.prompt: In an amine, the nitrogen carries two carbon groups and one hydrogen. What class of amine is it?

options.label: Secondary
Primary
Tertiary
Quaternary

items.explain: Secondary amines have two alkyl or aryl groups on the nitrogen, along with one hydrogen.

items.prompt: A nitrogen compound has its nitrogen attached to a carbonyl group, R−C(=O)−NR′R″. What is it called?

options.label: A tertiary amine
An amide
A quaternary ammonium salt
A cyclic amine

items.explain: Compounds where the nitrogen is attached to a carbonyl group are called amides.

items.prompt: A student compares ethylamine with ethyl alcohol at standard conditions. What does she find?

options.label: The amine is a liquid and the alcohol is a gas
Both are solids that melt only on heating
Both are gases that look the same
The amine is a gas and the alcohol is a liquid

items.explain: Methyl and ethyl amines are gases under standard conditions, whereas the corresponding alcohols are liquids.

items.prompt: Aniline dissolves poorly in water compared with a simple small amine. What best explains this?

options.label: Its lone pair is spread into the benzene ring, so it hydrogen-bonds less
Its lone pair is missing, so it cannot bond to anything at all
Its benzene ring adds an extra charge that repels water
Its amino group is tertiary, so it has no hydrogens to share

items.explain: In aromatic amines the lone pair is conjugated into the benzene ring, which diminishes hydrogen bonding, so water solubility is low.

items.prompt: A chemist sees two N–H bands in the infrared spectrum of an amine. What does that point to?

options.label: A secondary amine
A tertiary amine
A primary amine
A quaternary ammonium salt

items.explain: Primary amines show two N–H bands in the infrared spectrum, whereas secondary amines show only one.

items.prompt: A chemist writes N- in front of a group in an amine's name. What does it show?

options.label: That the amine contains only normal, straight chains
That the group is attached to the nitrogen atom
That the compound carries a net negative charge
That the molecule has more than one nitrogen atom

items.explain: The prefix N- shows substitution on the nitrogen atom.
